context: Animated chord diagram of global migration flows across 8 world regions and 5 decades (1970s–2010s), with a linked stacked area chart below showing net migration over time; controlled by a play/pause button and decade slider.
first_impression: The chord center is a genuine tangle at 8 regions × 56 ribbons, but the dark background and Tableau-10 palette keep it from feeling chaotic, and hover interaction (which dims unrelated ribbons to 0.08 opacity) would rescue legibility in practice.
what_works: The hover-highlight dimming strategy is well-executed — reducing non-hovered ribbons to near-invisible (0.08 opacity) effectively turns a 56-ribbon hairball into a focused 1-to-7 view on demand. The decade slider + linked area chart vertical highlight line is a clean two-view coordination that doesn't overload working memory.
what_doesnt: With all 56 ribbons at 0.55 opacity simultaneously, the chord center is an unreadable tangle at a glance — no clusters or dominant flows are identifiable without hovering, which means the at-rest state communicates little. The stacked area chart is cut off in the viewport as rendered (legend partially visible at bottom), and animation quality across 8 arcs + 56 ribbons transitioning simultaneously cannot be fully assessed from a static screenshot.
